changes: Marginal numbers below come from ablation: the full candidate minus a copy with that one rule switched off. P = PaddleOCR rgb_2x title exact-match count, given as dev/test. Ablation copies are in .runtime/poster-ocr/proposals-v2/title/ablate/<rule>/.

R1 name-prefix join (pattern a). A small name line directly above the title block is joined to it. It qualifies if (1) it has a year or edition marker plus 1-3 Hangul words, such as '2026 포천', '제29회 포천 산정호수' or '2026 노원 야외도서관', or (2) it is a single Hangul word of 2-6 characters, such as '경남고성', '양양' or '양천가족'. It must also have no festival suffix and no punctuation, height at least 0.2x the line below (with a marker) or 0.3x (without), sit inside that line's horizontal span, and touch it vertically. A line with a marker counts as the top of the block, so the climb stops there. The block may now hold 4 lines, with at most 3 same-size lines. Marginal P +1/+11; hybrid +1/+10; EasyOCR 2x 0/+5 (dev CER better).

R2 transparent marker and symbol lines. When the neighbour search hits a line that holds only a year or edition ('2026', '제3회'), or only symbols ('*'), it skips past it instead of stopping. Example: the '2026' next to '송이연어' no longer cuts off '양양'. Marginal P +1/+1.

R3 digit ratio on the stripped text. The 'mostly digits' filter is now measured after the year and edition are removed, so '2026 예천' and '2026포천' are no longer thrown out as number lines. Marginal P +1/+3.

R4 below-line policy (pattern b). A line ending in a suffix with at least 2 name letters in front of it ('강남청년축제', '제7회 안양 청년 축제') counts as a complete title. Nothing below it is appended, which stops slogans like '윗니스 소셜링', '청춘은 보라' and '첨년?너도용?'. Two exceptions: (1) a continuation line starting with & or × in the same script ('& 농산물 한마당'), and (2) a same-size line with a year and a place name ('NS푸드페스타 / 2026 익산'). A line that is only a suffix ('페스티벌') can still continue downward ('K-밀리터리 / 페스티벌 / 춘천대첩' is kept). As one group: P +1/+4, hybrid 0/+6. On its own the block is P 0/+4 (dev CER better), the joiner exception +1/0 (test CER better), the year+place exception +1/0.

R6 Korean over Latin (pattern c). If any Hangul candidate line ends in a festival suffix, Latin-only lines take a penalty of -2.7 instead of -1.2. Fixes 'TENSiON TIENUP FESTA' -> '동대문구 청소년 페스티벌' (dev v2-162). Marginal P +1 dev / 0 test exact. Test CER improves (v2-188 goes from the English variant to the Korean official, which OCR misread, '고등어죽제'), but title_any loses 1 on test. Hybrid +1 dev.

R7 misread edition marker. A token at the start of a word of the form 제 + 0-2 characters + 회 ('제크회', '제도회', '제근근회', '제회') is treated as an edition marker. It is removed from title.official, counts as a marker for R1/R2, and the edition number is not filled in. A guard keeps words like '제주회관'. title.official now goes through a single title_core(), which also strips '2026년' before the bare year. In v1 that order left a stray '년' in the title. Marginal P 0 dev / +3 test; hybrid 0/+2; EasyOCR 0/+1 (dev CER better).

R10 other edition forms. Native Korean ordinals ('첫 번째 이야기' = 1 ... '열 번째') and 'N주년' are read only when no 제N회, Nth or N번째 is present. An ordinal followed by 날, 일, 밤, 주 or 시간 is not an edition: '두 번째 날 공연' stays absent, as the existing test requires. Marginal edition P +1 dev / +2 test, and +1/+1 or +1/+2 on every other pipeline.
Infrastructure: ROOT now looks upward for data/festivals/poster.template.json. Without this the copy under .runtime cannot find the template. It has no effect when the file sits in app/poster_ocr.

Group results, P dev/test: assembly (R1-R4) +3/+16; edition handling (R7+R10) title 0/+3 and edition +1/+2. Full candidate against v1: P title +4/+18, edition +1/+2, core +2/+6. No title, edition, year, venue, schedule or list-field case got worse in exact match on any pipeline.

Tried and NOT included, because they do not improve both PaddleOCR splits. (1) More suffix words: (예술|영화|가요|음악|연극|국악|무용|아리랑|단오)제, 대전 after 2+ Hangul characters, 도서전. Test +1 on all 4 pipelines (v2-009), P dev 0. (2) Bonus for a title right after a year or edition line, plus excluding badge lines like '경기도 대표축제'. P 0/0 (test CER -0.0006); EasyOCR 2x title +1/+1 with dev CER 0.504 -> 0.470; hybrid dev +1. (3) A size reference that ignores short, low-confidence Latin noise: P 0/+1 (v2-025). (4) A confidence floor on joined lines (0.3 or 0.1): it broke EasyOCR, whose correct title lines often score 0.02-0.08, so it was dropped.

proposals.field_group: schedule: start/end dates, printed weekday, year basis, cross-line date ranges, operating times (schedule.times), duration_raw
changes: G0 (no effect on outputs): ROOT line replaced by the same PROPOSAL-SHIM the other proposals use, so the copy finds data/festivals/poster.template.json from .runtime/. Drop this line when merging into app/. The file is LF like extract_v1.py. change.diff was checked: applied to extract_v1.py it reproduces the candidate.

G1, read garbled date expressions (new D_* patterns; the v1 RANGE_RE/RANGE_NOSEP_RE/SINGLE_RE are kept unchanged for the venue code). (a) Unreadable weekday slot between the start date and the range sign: 2-3 mixed letter/digit chars ('5R1', '5at'), up to 4 chars in brackets ('(S00)', '(퇴)', '()'), or one symbol ('@', '©', '*', '°', '≠'). The slot is skipped and the weekday stays null. A legible Korean weekday char inside the noise is read ('1금|'). A bracketed weekday beats a bare char glued to the day ('16월(금)' -> fri). (b) The end-date weekday slot eats bracket noise ('8(입)'). (c) '/금' slash weekday. (d) An end month is read only if it is 1-12 ('~31.0' -> day 31). (e) New range signs: '→ ▶ ▸ _'. (f) Circled digits ①② are treated as a symbol '○', for date search only. NFKC had turned '12⑤' into '125'. (g) No-separator ranges also accept '|' and a date right after ')' ('3.(토)4.(일)'). Two dot-terminated dates ('09.18. 09.20.') are accepted with a noisy penalty. No characters are corrected and the calendar never fills a weekday. Group effect on pair (with vs without): PaddleOCR dev +1, test +13 (the later '|'/')' addition gave PaddleOCR test another +2); hybrid dev +4, test +4 (+3 from the '|'/')' addition); EasyOCR 2x test +4; EasyOCR 1x dev +1, test +5.

G2, date ranges split across lines. Two-line windows now also use the same-row right neighbour (a line split into two OCR records in swapped reading order) and the nearest line below in the same column. A strong one-line date no longer blocks the two-line window when the line ends with a range sign or the next line starts with one (up to 4 noise chars allowed before it: '2026.9.25.~' + '27.', '2026,9.18.' + 'FAI _ 20.'). Effect: PaddleOCR test pair +4, start_year +1, year +1. PaddleOCR dev pair unchanged, but year_basis improves 52 -> 55 of 58 (the year line is now joined to the date text). EasyOCR and hybrid dev pair +1 each (v2-041); all other pipelines improve on test.

G3, pairing consistency. (a) A single date that already sits inside a range on the same line is not paired ('10.16 (금)' + '10.17(토)-10.25'). (b) All pairs need similar text height (0.7-1.43); v1 required this only for weak pairs. This drops small notice dates such as a traffic-control '10.26'. (c) No pairs are formed inside a stacked list of 3 or more same-size date lines in one column (timetables, session lists). Effect: PaddleOCR pair dev +1, test +1; hybrid dev +1, test +2; EasyOCR test +2 (2x) and +2 (1x).

G4, multi-session union (extend_sessions). When the chosen schedule lines contain only dates, the period is widened to adjacent same-size date-only lines (within 1.5 line heights vertically and 6 horizontally, 120 days at most). Date-only means that after removing dates, weekdays, date labels and operating-day phrases ('매주 토,일', '주말', '평일', '매일') at most 2 letters remain. Effect: PaddleOCR pair dev +1 (v2-079), test +2; hybrid test +4; EasyOCR test +3 (2x) and +2 (1x).

G5, operating times (operating_times). (1) Time ranges on the schedule lines, plus a single 'HH:MM' on the start-date line ('5.(퇴)19:30'). Two 'HH:MM' separated only by a space count as one range. (2) Otherwise, time-only lines directly below or right of the schedule (chained down through further time-only lines), or lines with a time label (운영/관람/개방/오픈/입장/행사/축제 시간, OPEN, TIME, HOURS). (3) Otherwise all poster time ranges, but only if there are at most 2. This replaces 'every time range on the poster, first 6'. Effect on times F1: PaddleOCR dev 0.828 -> 1.000, test 0.730 -> 0.866; hybrid dev 0.500 -> 0.737, test 0.632 -> 0.702; EasyOCR 2x test 0.383 -> 0.408; EasyOCR 1x unchanged.

G6, schedule-line remainder used as the venue (pick_venue step 2). Dates are stripped with the D_* patterns, and time spans before dates ('10:00-21:00' used to leave '10: :00'). This stops the new schedule lines from leaking date or time fragments into the venue. Effect on venue: PaddleOCR dev +1, test +1. Without it, hybrid dev venue dropped by 1 (v2-196).

Rejected after testing: (a) pairs only between date-only lines: hurt EasyOCR and hybrid dev and test (date lines that carry a venue). (b) Height bonus relative to the largest date candidate: PaddleOCR dev 0, test pair +1 but weekday -1. (c) No calendar bonus for a '일' suffix read as Sunday: no effect anywhere. (d) Filling weekday from the calendar: the schema says it must not be computed.

proposals.field_group: venue raw/items, address, admin_area (scored as venue, venue_partial, address, admin_district, plus presence of venue/address/admin_area)
changes: Row-neighbour merge (row_neighbors). build_lines only attaches records to the right, so a left record with a slightly lower centre ('서천군 홍원항' + '일원 (…)'), or a fragment sitting between two records, ended up as a separate line. A line is now joined to the chosen venue line when they overlap vertically by at least 60%, have similar height (0.75-1.33, or 0.5-1.5 for a '(' line or a line with a venue word) and sit close together horizontally, and the neighbour has no date, year, role, phone, title suffix or address. Ablation on PaddleOCR: dev venue +1, test venue +8 and admin +2.

Column-based up/down continuation (column_line + continuation). This replaces v1's index±1 neighbour, which picked lines from a parallel column that fell between the two in reading order. A line that overlaps vertically with the venue box by more than half its height (for example a giant title) is not a neighbour. A neighbour is joined if it ends with a joiner, is a '(' caption, or contains a venue word (0.75-1.33 height, aligned). It is not joined if it is an address line, a Latin-only translation, or contains a date; when a line contains a date, only its leading segment is joined, and only if that segment has a venue word. The VENUE_WORD path now needs a height ratio of at least 0.75. Fixes trailing junk such as v2-009/024/147/174 and two-line venues such as v2-128/190/056/021.

Short prefix/suffix lines without a venue word (for example '영동 레인보우' / '힐링관광지 일원', '벽골제 중심') are joined only when they are tightly stacked: 0.85-1.18 height ratio, a gap of at most 0.3 line, at most 10 Hangul characters and 3 words, aligned left, right or centre. Ablation on PaddleOCR: dev venue_partial +1, test venue +6, core_all +3.

VENUE_WORD refinement. Short words that often sit inside other words (궁, 홀, 섬, 숲, 월드, 랜드, 마당) now count only at the end of a word, and '아트' alone no longer counts; this removes 홀리데이, 브랜드, 미디어아트 and 궁금 false hits. Added 전역, 축제장, 행사장, 주차장, 야영장, 시네마, 영화관 and '(시|군|구)청 앞'. Latin words PARK, Hall, Center, Square, Stadium, Plaza, Arena, Museum and Theater count at word boundaries. Hangul options are preferred over Latin-only ones, and 일원/일대/전역 lines over others. Ablation on PaddleOCR: dev 0, test venue +7 and admin +2; positive on every pipeline.

Tail cut (cut_venue_tail inside clean_venue). The text is cut at a phone number, at contact marks (문의, 전화, TEL, ☎, 홈페이지, www, http) and at role marks (주최, 주관, …), and a trailing Latin translation of 2 or more words outside parentheses is dropped. A leading lone 'I', 'l' or '|' separator token is also stripped. Ablation: PaddleOCR dev venue_partial +1, test venue +1; hybrid dev venue +1 and core +1.

Safe date stripping in venue text (date_spans, strip_dates_safe, date_segments). This replaces v1's strip_dates and DATE_RESIDUE. changes: How changes were accepted: a change is kept only if, at the level of its field, it improves PaddleOCR dev AND test separately. Every sub-rule inside a kept field also has to be >= 0 on all 4 pipelines x 2 splits (checked by leave-one-out ablation). Sub-rules whose own effect falls on only one split are marked below so the merger can drop them if it wants per-rule strictness.

ORG-1 (first name cell after a bare role label): the gap allowed after a label with no name in the same record goes from 2.5x to ORG_FIRST_GAP=4.5x the label height, because a logo sits in between (e.g. '후원 [logo]영천시 주관 [logo]대구한의대학교'). That cell may also be a taller logo text, up to ORG_TALL=3.0x the label height (old limit 1.8). The gap part alone gives Paddle test +4 TP; the tall part alone gives Paddle dev +1 TP. The result is flat for gap 4-6 and tall 2.6-3.5.

ORG-2 (low-confidence names): a name whose own OCR records have confidence < ORG_MIN_CONF=0.5 (same threshold for every engine) is output as name=null, legibility=illegible, with role and role_raw kept. The schema and validator already allow this, and poster.py flags it as role_name_unclear for human review. No characters are changed. This removes garbled names: Paddle FP dev 31->28, test 54->47 (counted with ORG-1 on); EasyOCR 2x test 19->4; hybrid test 26->11. No TP lost on any pipeline. issues.location: Overall evidence: candidate vs extract_v1, all hunks
issues.problem: Gains are lopsided toward test, which suggests most v2 rules were derived from test failures, so test is no longer a held-out estimate. Several hunks have zero PaddleOCR dev effect (see S2, V4, S3a/S3c and the single-case items below).
issues.fix: Report test numbers as development numbers, not generalization. Treat the r2-* reserve as the only unbiased number and expect reserve gains closer to the dev-sized deltas. Freeze VERSION and rules before running the reserve once.

issues.problem: This rule fires on exactly one poster, dev v2-138 (PaddleOCR and hybrid). Disabling it alone changes only v2-138 (title and admin_district). It is a case patch inside the otherwise general 'stop below a complete ○○축제 title' rule.

issues.problem: This rule fires on one poster, test v2-145 ('10월 16월(금)~ 18일(일)'). Disabling it changes only that case. It also overrides an already-read weekday char ('월') with the bracketed one, which in effect encodes the OCR misread 일->월. That is borderline character correction.
issues.fix: Remove the gb/gbw alternative and the gbw override in _read_weekday. Keep gw/ga/gs: they fire on 2-3 posters across engines.

issues.problem: The native-ordinal part ('첫 번째') fires only on dev v2-144. The 'N주년' part has no dev evidence; on test it gives 2 tp (v2-126, v2-133) and 1 fp on every engine (v2-109 '제76주년 춘천지구전투 전승행사' -> edition 76). An anniversary is not an edition: N주년 is usually edition N+1, or an unrelated anniversary (battle, founding).
issues.fix: Drop EDITION_ALT entirely (net effect: dev -1, test -2+1 fp per engine). If kept, restrict 주년 to lines that also contain a TITLE_SUFFIX, and document the 회차 label convention in the poster standard first.

issues.problem: These thresholds were tuned on a single dev poster: dev evidence is only v2-162 (ORG_TALL, '동대문구'). On PaddleOCR test the first-gap rule adds 4 tp and 7 fp (v2-051 '민구경역시', v2-105 '주권' x2, v2-109 '대한민국 국명무'/'2군단', v2-121 '시리오', v2-194). Precision of the new items is 36%. Org F1 only rises because base precision is very low.
issues.fix: Revert to 2.5 and 1.8 (drop both constants). If logo-gap handling is wanted, require the far cell to pass INSTITUTION_BODY or a district suffix rather than widening the gap.

issues.problem: Presence precision regresses. PaddleOCR admin_area fp: dev 0->2, test 4->14 (V8 alone: test tp +8, fp +9; dev tp +2, fp +2). Hybrid test fp 4->8, EasyOCR 2x test 2->4. The gold is inconsistent for bare city names in titles. Labelled present: 영천한방축제, 정선야행, 화순고인돌, '2026 익산'. Labelled absent: 부천국제만화축제, 강남청년축제, 경주국가유산야행, 청주의보물, '2026대덕', 안산, 서산, 서귀포. No geometric or token restriction separates the two groups; I checked spaced vs glued. Also '제주레저' gives district=제주 where gold has region=제주.
issues.fix: Settle the label rule first ('장소·제목 문구에 직접 쓰인 지역명만' arguably covers bare stems) and relabel the inconsistent gold. Until then, drop V8 or report the admin_area precision loss explicitly next to the admin_district gain (+2 dev, +6 test). It is not acceptable under the 'does not regress by more than it helps' rule on presence.

issues.problem: This rule fires on one poster (test v2-146 '(금)|18.(일)'). Disabling it changes only that case.

issues.problem: This rule fires on one poster (test v2-116 '10.09./금'), and the only effect is start_weekday on that poster in all 4 pipelines.

issues.problem: The '.'-thousands rule fires only on dev v2-113 ('65,500.000원') and reinterprets an OCR '.' as ','. issues.fix: Drop the [,.] thousands branch (use (?:,\d{3})+). Set total_krw=None when an 억 amount has 4+ unseparated digits before 억, or exceeds a fixed cap. Keep raw.

issues.problem: On PaddleOCR dev, venue accuracy is unchanged (41->41), and presence tp drops 1 (v2-099, which was a garbage v1 hit '궁문화속진'). Test gains +7. The word-end restriction for 궁/홀/섬/숲/월드/랜드 and dropping bare '아트' are good general precision fixes (removes 미추홀구, 홀리데이, 브랜드, 궁중 hits).
issues.fix: Keep the word-end restrictions and the generic Korean nouns (축제장, 행사장, 마당$, 전역). Drop or justify dead entries and the English list. Do not cite V4 as dev-validated.

Also, garbled edition markers are accepted as names: '제근근회' causes the v2-060 title loss and '제회' affects v2-038. Otherwise T1 is a sound general layout rule: 27 PaddleOCR firings with CER improvement almost everywhere.
issues.fix: Use one floor (.3), or document why marked lines may be smaller. Treat tokens shaped like 제\S{0,3}회 as markers, not name tokens, in name_tokens/has_marker. Ignoring a token is not character correction.

issues.fix: Remove both. Keep CONTACT_MARK/PHONE/ROLE tail cutting (test v2-061) and the general LATIN_TRAIL (dev v2-192).

issues.problem: The merged candidate fails 2 of the venue proposal's own unit tests. issues.problem: Catastrophic backtracking. In `(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z.'\-]*\s*){2,}$` the `\s*` can be empty, so any run of N Latin letters can be split 2^(N-1) ways. When `$` then fails (a digit, Korean text or '(' after the English), the time doubles with each extra letter: 22 letters take 0.28 s. The realistic venue line '장소: 올림픽공원 Olympic Park Seoul Korea Main Stadium Hall 1층' took 148.6 s in extract(), and a few more letters would hang it for hours. Bilingual venue lines like this are common, so the reserve set or production could stall even though dev/test did not.
issues.fix: Use a linear form that accepts the same strings: `(?<=[가-힣)])\s*(?:[|/]|\s[Il])?\s+(?=[A-Za-z][^A-Za-z]*[A-Za-z])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z.'\-]*(?:\s+[A-Za-z][A-Za-z.'\-]*)*\s*$`. On 300k random strings its match spans equal the old pattern's (0 mismatches). It now runs in 0.0 ms, and all dev/test predictions are byte-identical to the merged candidate. Applied in review/fixed/extract.py.

issues.location: merged/extract.py:715-716 (extract) and extend_sessions hi_pt (line ~519); new path in v2
issues.problem: Cross-year session blocks end before they start. For '2026.12.20.(일)~12.24.(목)' followed by '12.30.(수)~1.3.(일)', extend_sessions builds an end point with no year (or, when that line has a year, with the start year). extract then fills `end = point(start["year"], ...)` without moving to the next year, so the output is start 2026-12-20, end 2026-01-03. The document is schema-valid but wrong, and poster_findings would raise date_order. v1 did not extend sessions, so it did not hit this.
issues.fix: In extend_sessions use `point(de.year if (d["ey"] or d["sy"]) else None, ...)` for hi_pt. In extract's `elif end["year"] is None` branch use `e_year = start["year"] + 1 if (end month, day) < (start month, day) else start["year"]`. The synthetic case now gives 2027-01-03, with 0 prediction changes on dev/test.

issues.problem: Crash: TypeError 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable when the poster year is a common year and the chosen date is a 2.29 with no year printed (e.g. '2026' plus '2.29(일)'). pick_schedule only checks that the date exists for ranges; for a single date, extract's point(poster_year, 2, 29) returns None, and line 728 then reads start['year'].

No current run has a null confidence, but a VLM or hybrid source could produce one.

issues.problem: The comment says 'two or more English words', but because of the empty `\s*` a single word of 2+ letters also matches. So '광장 Ab' becomes '광장', '올림픽공원 KSPO' becomes '올림픽공원', and '/ S.E.D' is dropped.

issues.problem: cut_venue_tail treats any '문의' as a contact label, which also cuts real place names: '청주 문의면 청남대 일원' becomes '청주'. This does not occur in dev/test.
issues.fix: Only cut when '문의' is followed by a contact token, e.g. `문\s*의(?=\s*(?:처|사항|전화|[:：☎(]|\d|$))`, or exclude a following 면/동/리.

issues.problem: The comment says '한마당' is not accepted as a venue word, but the regex matches it ('주민 한마당' hits VENUE_WORD). The TITLE_SUFFIX filters currently hide this.
issues.fix: Use `(?<!한)마당(?![가-힣])`, or correct the comment.

issues.problem: When the earliest session line has no year but the block's year comes from date text, start.year_basis becomes 'poster_text' instead of 'date_text'. Example: '10.2.(금)' + '2026.10.3.(토)~4.(일)'. Schema-valid, but the provenance is wrong.
issues.fix: Carry c['sy'] into lo_pt/hi_pt when the extending line has no year (basis 'date_text').

issues.problem: These patterns are quadratic on very long single lines because they have no left anchor. A 20k-character line takes 3–15 s each. Real OCR lines are under 300 characters, and v1 behaves the same.
issues.fix: Optional: add left boundaries (e.g. `(?<![가-힣0-9])` for ROAD/JIBUN, which does not change the first match) or cap line length before matching.

extras.recommendation:
Yes, ship v2 as a fused pipeline, but only a same-engine one: PaddleOCR rgb_2x as primary plus PaddleOCR rgb_1x as secondary. It uses four general slot rules and no gold, file names or character edits:
1. Title: keep whichever variant's cited OCR lines have the higher mean recognition confidence. Confidence is comparable here because both readings come from the same engine.
2. Edition: take rgb_1x's edition when rgb_1x has one.
3. Organisations: take the whole list from rgb_1x.
4. Any other slot that rgb_2x left absent: fill it from rgb_1x (this is what fusion.py already does).

On both splits it improves core_all, title, title_any, edition, organisations F1 and contacts F1. No field drops on either split: venue and year are unchanged, and schedule_pair is unchanged on dev and up 1 on test. Average OCR time per poster rises by 44% (39.9 s to 57.6 s). It uses the same model, needs no second engine or model load, and peak memory stays at the rgb_2x level when the two runs are sequential.

Do not fuse with EasyOCR or the hybrid pipeline as override voters or per-field sources. They lose many more cases than they gain:
- 3-way vote: dev core drops 18 to 15.
- Venue taken from hybrid: dev venue drops 37 to 31.
- Organisations taken from EasyOCR or hybrid: F1 falls.
- Edition taken from hybrid: dev +3, test -1.

Hybrid as an absent-slot fallback (fusion_ph) never loses a case, but it gains only 7 field-cases. For that it adds a second engine, about 1.5 GB of memory, 13 s of model load and +33% time. Not worth it. The one hybrid use that improves both splits is a schedule vote among Paddle 2x, Paddle 1x and hybrid 2x: dev +2/-0 and test +6/-2 on schedule_pair, but test year drops by 1. Keep that only as an option if the product already runs hybrid.

Caveats:
- None of the gains is significant on its own.
- About 50 policies were tried on dev+test, so the chosen one should be confirmed once on reserve together with the frozen v2 rules.
- Rebuild it as a per-slot policy in app/poster_ocr/fusion.py and re-measure after rule v2 is fixed. These numbers are with v1 rules, and several title gains come from region-prefix line grouping that v2 rules might absorb.
- Fusion adds at most +2 to +3 points. The v1 dev-to-test drop is far larger (title 38% to 25%, core 33% to 5%), so generalising the rules matters much more than fusion.

The proposal is at C:\Users\playdata2\Desktop\SKN33-Final-1Team\SKN33-Final-1Team\.runtime\poster-ocr\proposals-v2\schema\proposal.md. The scripts that reproduce it (load.py, gaz.py, admin.py, sim.py) are in the same folder; gaz.py's district list is for labelling and scoring only, never the extractor.

Findings:
(1) admin_area is the worst offender. Labellers used two conventions: 25 notes require an administrative suffix, while 13 notes accept bare names (pass 2 switched only some files). Bare city/district names also inside compound words split the same way (예산사과축제 is labelled present, 예산장터 absent). The blind labels disagree on 8/30 cases (27%). Rule A1 counts a district only when it is a standalone token carrying the 시/군/구 suffix, and a 시·도 only from a closed list. It can be applied by script and changes 53 files (dev 13, test 40); 2 files (v2-002, v2-024) need an image check and should stay as they are. With the current extractor, PaddleOCR district accuracy goes from 11/25 to 11/15 on dev and from 14/63 to 14/26 on test. The number of correct answers does not change: the removed labels were ones a dictionary-free extractor could never reach. Presence recall rises (0.53→0.75 dev, 0.35→0.65 test) and precision falls (1.00→0.88 dev, 0.86→0.76 test), because the extractor's 시·도 regex has no word boundary.
(2) title.official already follows "raw minus year and edition" in 200/200 files, and region prefixes are included consistently. Titles starting with a region name make up 20% of dev but 42% of test, which explains part of the v1 title drop. I propose an extra score, title_core (also accepts a match once the leading region/place word is removed), with title staying the main score. PaddleOCR title_any goes 24→25 on dev and 41→49 on test; hybrid 21→21 and 28→33. The two blind title disagreements both concern lines above the title (genre or event-type labels), so rule T1 needs to be written down.
(3) In 12 files the English/brand variants keep the year or edition. Scoring should strip them; this has no effect on current predictions.
(4) venue.raw: an address in parentheses after the place name is included in 4 files and excluded in 3, depending on print layout; English translations in parentheses are also inconsistent. Rule V1 drops the address part and the English translation, changing 5 test files. With the current extractor, PaddleOCR and hybrid each lose 1 test case. Simulated together with a small extractor rule (drop a trailing parenthesis that matches the detected address), PaddleOCR goes 37→38 dev and 59→59 test, hybrid 28→29 and 48→49, so V1 should only be adopted together with that rule.
(5) organizations: 239 of 395 named, role-labelled gold items are marked partial (some characters uncertain), and no pipeline matches any of them. Scoring F1 on legible items only raises PaddleOCR F1 from 0.076 to 0.128 on dev and 0.072 to 0.148 on test. I also propose written rules for name granularity (blind v2-156), role inheritance across wrapped lines, and an optional role_status field for 4 files where a role label is printed but unreadable.
(6) schedule: across the 16 multi-period files the gold applies an unwritten priority order with no exceptions: labelled overall period first, then the sub-event whose name matches the title, then the full span, with pre-events going to programs. No gold changes are needed; PaddleOCR misses 6 of these (dev 1, test 5) by picking the first interval. I propose recording the separate intervals in operating_raw for 3 files (v2-006, v2-121, v2-143); v2-079 is partly done.
The rule-based gold changes (57 files including the overlap) can also be applied to the reserve set by script without anyone opening it.

proposals.problem: Two conventions are mixed across the gold. 25 labeller notes require a 시/군/구 suffix ('진안' has no suffix → absent); 13 notes, including some pass-2 edits, accept bare names (포천, 양양) or names inside compounds (예산사과축제 present but 예산장터 absent). Region short forms inside compounds are also split: 부산불꽃축제 and 광주서창 are labelled present, 세종한글축제 and 서울어린이대공원 absent; '울산 야외도서관' is absent while '대전 빵 축제' is present. Blind disagreement is 8/30 (27%). A dictionary-free extractor cannot reach bare-name labels: PaddleOCR gets 0 of them right.
proposals.rule: A1 (standard 1.1): sources are the title block, venue block and address line only (not organisations, logos or slogans). Region comes from a closed 시·도 list (full name, short form, ○○시/○○도, 전남광주통합특별시; Hangul only). District requires a full name with 시/군/구/특례시 suffix. Each must be a standalone token, or part of a token made only of admin units (대전중구); a trailing 일원/일대/전역 is allowed. Bare names (포천) and names inside compounds (예산사과축제, 남구청년예술제, 성북구청, 태백시청, 부산불꽃축제) do not count. Values are written as printed, sources checked in order venue → address → title; multiple districts are joined by a space when adjacent and by ', ' when separate. Script-applicable from title.raw, venue.raw, address.raw plus the official district list (labelling only). v2-002 and v2-024 need an image check and should stay present. PaddleOCR rgb_2x district accuracy: dev 11/25→11/15, test 14/63→14/26; presence recall 0.53→0.75 (dev) and 0.35→0.65 (test); precision 1.00→0.88 and 0.86→0.76.

proposals.problem: official = raw minus year and edition holds in 200/200 files, and region prefixes attached to the title are included consistently (71 titles: dev 12, test 59). Which lines above the title belong to it is not specified, though: genre, event-type and occasion lines. Both blind title disagreements are of this kind (v2-016 '창작 실경뮤지컬', v2-052 '청년 STREET페스티벌'). Related cases: v2-001, v2-025, v2-090.
proposals.rule: T1 (labelling, needs human judgement): title.raw holds every line printed as part of the title lockup, in reading order. Include region/place prefixes (small, speech-bubble or vertical text too), qualifiers (세계문화유산, 가을) and continuations with &, in or × in the same block. Exclude genre/format-only lines, '…기념' occasion lines and region tags printed apart from the title; record an excluded line that contains the festival name as variants[alias]. official stays raw minus year minus edition. No gold changes.

proposals.problem: The extractor drops a leading region prefix in 9 PaddleOCR cases (dev 1, test 8). These are scored the same as completely wrong titles, and prefixed titles are twice as common in test as in dev.
proposals.rule: T3 (evaluate.py, extra score; keep title as the main score): title_core counts as correct when title_any matches, or when gold official/variants and the prediction match after removing a leading standalone admin word (시·도, suffixed 시·군·구 or bare 시·군·구 name; the list is used only in scoring). PaddleOCR rgb_2x title_any → title_core: dev 24→25, test 41→49. Hybrid 21→21 / 28→33; easyocr rgb_2x 12→12 / 15→18; easyocr rgb_1x 11→11 / 16→19. No gold changes.

proposals.problem: official strips year and edition, but 13 variants in 12 files keep them ('Hyoseok Cultural Festival 2026', 'The 12th Muan …'), while v2-041's note strips them. title_any could therefore reject an English title extracted correctly without the year.
proposals.rule: T4 (evaluate.py): before comparing title_any/title_core, remove 4-digit years (2026, 2026년) and edition tokens (제N회, The Nth, Nst/nd/rd/th) from the variants. variants[].raw stays the printed text. No effect on current predictions; no gold changes.

proposals.problem: 7 files have only a Latin-script title and keep it as official, which is consistent. Bilingual posters use the Korean title as official (v2-020 note). v2-125 keeps the large English title because its Korean name is printed in scattered pieces.
proposals.rule: T2: if Korean and English festival names are both printed as a single block, official is the Korean one and the English goes to variants[english]. If the Korean name is scattered or there is no Korean, official is the Latin text as printed. No changes; v2-125 needs a team decision.

proposals.problem: An address in parentheses or after a separator is part of venue.raw in 4 files (v2-005, 016, 137, 176) and excluded in 3 (v2-089, 157, 174); the deciding factor was print layout, which the gold does not record. English translations in parentheses are kept in v2-023 but dropped in v2-125 and v2-192.
proposals.rule: V1: venue.raw is the venue phrase (region prefix, 일원/일대 and descriptive parentheses kept) minus the venue label (장소/위치/Venue/@/pin), minus any address part attached by parentheses or a separator (the address goes in address.raw only), minus a Latin-only translation in parentheses when the main text is Korean. If the venue text is only an address, keep it whole. Script-applicable: 5 test files change. With the current extractor PaddleOCR goes dev 37→37 and test 59→58, hybrid 28→28 and 48→47, easyocr unchanged. Combined with an extractor rule that drops a trailing parenthesis equal to the detected address (simulated on saved predictions, not implemented): PaddleOCR 38 / 59, hybrid 29 / 49. Adopt only together with that extractor rule.

proposals.problem: 239 of 395 named, role-labelled gold items (dev 56/98, test 183/297, in 70 files) are marked partial (some characters uncertain). The exact-match F1 counts all of them as misses, and no pipeline matches any of them (PaddleOCR 0/204 partial logos, 0/35 partial text), so org recall mostly measures labeller uncertainty.

Partial items are ignored: a prediction matching one is neither a hit nor a false positive (optionally reported separately with a character-error-rate match). proposals.field: organizations (name granularity, role inheritance, unlabelled logos)
proposals.problem: Mapping from printed role label to roles is 100% consistent, and the 220 items without a role label (84 files) correctly have roles=[]. But there is no rule for splitting names: gold keeps '합천군 황매산축제위원회' as one organisation while the blind label split it into two (v2-156), and there are 8 similar plus 12 '시·도 + district' names. Role inheritance across wrapped lines (v2-019, 130, 147) is unwritten. A role label that is printed but unreadable (v2-077, 146, 152, 166) looks the same as no label, so the 'roles_unlabeled' check reports it wrongly.
proposals.rule: O2: one item per printed organisation. A region/district name and an institution name on one logo or line without a separator form one name; split only on ·, /, comma, 및, |, × or separate logos; the same organisation printed under different roles becomes separate items. O3: a role label applies to its line and to wrapped continuation lines of the same list, until the next role label or band; logos in a separate unlabelled band keep roles=[]. O4 (optional schema change): role_status = labeled | unlabeled | illegible, set to illegible in 4 files. No metric effect; no current gold changes except O4.

proposals.problem: The standard does not say how to choose the main period when several date blocks are printed. The 16 gold files with multiple blocks follow an unwritten priority order with no exceptions. PaddleOCR predictions follow a different choice (first interval or a sub-block) in 6 of them (dev v2-079; test v2-006, 098, 116, 119, 143): these are extractor errors, not gold inconsistency.
proposals.rule: S1: a labelled overall period (축제기간, 행사기간, 기간, 일시, 본행사, 운영기간, 운영일정) wins. S2: otherwise, if the blocks are named sub-events and one name equals or is contained in title.official (ignoring spaces and punctuation), use that block. S3: otherwise use the full span (first start to last end) of all date phrases of the same event. S4: eve/pre-events printed outside the main period (전야제, 개막제, 사전행사, 추모제) and co-held separate events go to programs[].period. Exceptions: composite image v2-097, lineup poster v2-111. No gold changes.

proposals.problem: When separate intervals or dates are merged into one span, only v2-116 records the printed date list in operating_raw. v2-006, v2-121 and v2-143 leave it empty and v2-079 has only '매주 토,일', so the span can be mistaken for daily operation. The field is not scored.
proposals.rule: S5: whenever schedule is an S3 span over separate intervals or dates, operating_raw holds the printed interval/date list (labels removed). Optional schema addition: schedule.basis = labeled | title_block | span | single, so span cases can be scored separately. No metric effect.
